input.question: Why is gold worth more than silver?
input.ground_truth: Originally, because Gold was rarer, therefore harder to get hold of: the standard rule of supply and demand means that a rarer metal, where both are in demand, will be more expensive. Nowadays, silver is actually rarer, but the perception has been, for hundreds of years, that gold is rarer and more expensive... so there's a higher demand for gold. That means that although gold has greater supply than silver, the demand for gold is still significantly higher: enough that the price stays higher. **If you have 10 pieces of silver, and 20 pieces of gold, but 10 people want the silver and 30 people want the gold... which will you get a higher price for?**

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why is gold worth more than silver?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have two toys: one is a shiny, super special toy that everyone wants, and the other is also shiny but not as special to most people.

Gold is like the super special toy. A long, long time ago, people decided gold is really pretty and they want it a lot. So, many people want to have gold, but there isn’t as much gold as there is of other shiny things like silver.

Because not many people can find gold, and lots of people want it, people are willing to give more toys (which we call “money”) to get gold than to get silver.

So, that’s why gold is worth more than silver!
